question: What is Connecticut's baseline life jacket requirement for every vessel on the water?
choice_a: Only the operator needs a life jacket; passengers do not
choice_b: Life jackets are only required on vessels longer than 26 feet
choice_c: Life jackets are optional as long as the boat carries a throwable cushion
choice_d: A wearable life jacket that is readily accessible and properly fits the intended wearer must be aboard for each person on the vessel
explanation: Connecticut law requires a wearable life jacket for each person aboard every vessel, and each one must be readily accessible and properly fit the person who would wear it.
source_note: 2026 CT DEEP Boater's Guide, "Connecticut Life Jacket and Personal Flotation Device (PFD) Laws," p.17

question: Under Connecticut law, when must life jackets be worn (not just carried) by children under 13 years old aboard a vessel that is underway?
choice_a: At all times, unless the child is below deck or in an enclosed cabin
choice_b: Only when the vessel is anchored
choice_d: Never -- carrying one aboard is always sufficient regardless of age
explanation: Connecticut requires children under 13 to wear a life jacket at all times while a vessel is underway, unless they are below deck or in an enclosed cabin.
source_note: 2026 CT DEEP Boater's Guide, "Connecticut Life Jacket and Personal Flotation Device (PFD) Laws," p.17

question: What does Connecticut law require regarding life jackets on manually propelled vessels (kayaks, canoes, rowboats) each year from October 1 through May 31?
choice_a: No life jacket is required on manually propelled vessels at any time of year
choice_b: Every person aboard a manually propelled vessel must wear a life jacket during that period, regardless of age
choice_c: Only children need to wear a life jacket during that period
choice_d: Life jackets need only be worn if the water temperature exceeds 70 degrees
explanation: Every year from October 1st through May 31st, life jackets must be worn by anyone in or operating a manually propelled vessel, reflecting the elevated cold-water risk in Connecticut's colder months.
source_note: 2026 CT DEEP Boater's Guide, "Connecticut Life Jacket and Personal Flotation Device (PFD) Laws," p.17

question: Under Connecticut law, in addition to wearable life jackets for each person, what must all vessels 16 feet and over also carry?
choice_b: A spare anchor of at least 20 pounds
choice_c: A Type IV throwable device, in addition to the required number of wearable life jackets
choice_d: Nothing additional beyond the wearable life jackets
explanation: Connecticut law requires all vessels 16 feet and over to carry a Type IV throwable device, such as a buoyant cushion or ring buoy, on top of the wearable life jacket required for each person aboard.
source_note: 2026 CT DEEP Boater's Guide, "Connecticut Life Jacket and Personal Flotation Device (PFD) Laws," p.17

question: Which of the following is NOT a legal substitute for a proper life jacket under Connecticut law?
choice_a: A U.S. Coast Guard approved Type III vest
choice_b: A U.S. Coast Guard approved Type II horse-collar device
choice_c: A U.S. Coast Guard approved inflatable Type V vest (used within its label restrictions)
explanation: Connecticut's Boater's Guide specifically states that ski belts are not legal life jackets, regardless of how snugly they fit, because they are not U.S. Coast Guard approved as a personal flotation device.
source_note: 2026 CT DEEP Boater's Guide, "Connecticut Life Jacket and Personal Flotation Device (PFD) Laws," p.17

question: Under Connecticut law, who is prohibited from using an inflatable life jacket while engaged in high-speed water sports such as riding a PWC or water skiing?
choice_a: Persons weighing under 90 lbs. or under 16 years of age
choice_d: No one -- inflatables are always allowed for any water sport
explanation: Inflatable life jackets may not be used by persons engaged in high-speed water sports like PWC riding or water skiing if they weigh under 90 lbs. or are under 16 years of age; inflatables are also never approved for PWC use at all under Connecticut's PWC-specific rules.
source_note: 2026 CT DEEP Boater's Guide, "Connecticut Life Jacket and Personal Flotation Device (PFD) Laws," p.17

question: What must every life jacket meet to be legal in Connecticut, according to the Boater's Guide's life jacket requirements?
choice_a: It only needs to be brightly colored
choice_b: It must be U.S. Coast Guard approved, have a legible label, and be in serviceable condition with intact straps, buckles, seams, and material
choice_c: It only needs to float, regardless of approval status
choice_d: It must be less than one year old regardless of condition
explanation: Connecticut requires life jackets to be U.S. Coast Guard approved, carry a legible label, and be in serviceable condition -- meaning all straps, buckles, seams, and material are intact and functional.
source_note: 2026 CT DEEP Boater's Guide, "Connecticut Life Jacket and Personal Flotation Device (PFD) Laws," p.17

question: What does the newer performance-level life jacket labeling system (used alongside the older Type I-V system) indicate?
choice_a: The exact retail price of the life jacket
choice_b: Whether the life jacket is machine washable
choice_c: A performance level measured in newtons, where a lower number favors mobility and comfort near shore and a higher number offers greater flotation and stability for offshore use
explanation: The newer performance-level labels (approved for use in both the U.S. and Canada) rate flotation in newtons; a lower performance level favors mobility and comfort for near-shore, calm-water activities, while a higher level provides greater flotation, turning ability, and stability for offshore conditions where rescue may take longer.
source_note: 2026 CT DEEP Boater's Guide, "New Life Jacket Labels," p.22

question: According to Connecticut's Boater's Guide, which activities are certain life jackets specifically NOT approved for, even though the jacket is otherwise USCG-approved?
choice_d: Water skiing, tubing, personal watercraft or wakeboarding, and white-water paddling, depending on the specific jacket's label warnings
explanation: The Boater's Guide's life jacket selection chart warns that some life jackets are not approved for activities like water skiing, tubing, PWC use or wakeboarding, and white-water paddling, and that some designs will not turn an unconscious wearer face-up -- boaters should always check the specific label before use.
source_note: 2026 CT DEEP Boater's Guide, "Choose the Right Life Jacket," p.22

question: Under federal exemptions recognized in Connecticut, which manually propelled craft are exempted from carrying the PFD otherwise required under 33 CFR 175.15?
choice_a: Racing shells, rowing sculls, racing canoes, and racing kayaks
choice_b: Standard recreational kayaks used for fishing
choice_d: Any vessel operated by an adult
explanation: Under 33 CFR 175.17's narrow exemptions, racing shells, rowing sculls, racing canoes, and racing kayaks are exempted from carrying the PFD that would otherwise be required under 33 CFR 175.15, reflecting their specialized competitive design.
source_note: 2026 CT DEEP Boater's Guide, "Manually Propelled Vessel Regulations," p.36, citing 33 CFR 175.17

question: Water skiers towed behind a Connecticut vessel are required by law to wear a U.S. Coast Guard approved life jacket while skiing, with what narrow exceptions?
choice_a: Any skier who says they are a strong swimmer
choice_b: Barefoot skiers wearing a specifically designed barefoot wetsuit, and trick skiers on standard double trick skis under specific size and towing-speed conditions
choice_c: Skiers under the age of 10 only
choice_d: There are no exceptions of any kind
explanation: Connecticut law requires water skiers to wear a USCG-approved life jacket except for barefoot skiers wearing a specifically designed barefoot wetsuit, and trick skiers on standard double trick skis at least eight inches wide and no more than 46 inches long being towed at not more than 20 mph on a tow rope over 50 feet; even then, a life jacket must be kept readily available aboard the tow vessel.
source_note: 2026 CT DEEP Boater's Guide, "Water Skiing and Parasailing," p.26
